root_cause.text: The bpf_prog_test_run_skb() function fails to validate that the L3 header (IPv4/IPv6) is fully present in the skb head before dereferencing ip_hdr() or ipv6_hdr() when the protocol switch handles those EtherTypes, allowing an out-of-bounds read if the test input only contains an Ethernet header.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the length check (e.g., `if (skb_headlen(skb) < sizeof(struct iphdr))`) before accessing the IP header fields, and returns -EINVAL if the check fails. The commit message explicitly states: "it may access ip_hdr(skb) or ipv6_hdr(skb) even when the provided test input only contains an Ethernet header." The diff shows the original code had a conditional assignment after the access, but the access itself was not guarded.

candidates.rationale: The switch statement dispatches to IP or IPv6 cases without any prior validation that the L3 header is present in the skb linear data.
This case enters the IP handling path where ip_hdr() will be dereferenced, but there is no guarantee that the IP header is fully present in the skb head.
Setting the socket family before verifying that the IP header is present allows the subsequent dereference to occur on potentially incomplete data.
